contributions: Six MLOps principles: automation, versioning, experiment tracking, testing, monitoring, reproducibility

practices: Progress from manual process to continuous training (triggered on schedule, new data or a monitoring drop) to CI/CD; CT automates the FTI pipelines, CI/CD ships new pipeline code (1. Automation).
Version code (Git, semantic releases), models (registry with metadata store) and data (SQL version column, DVC or artifacts) separately (2. Versioning).
Log experiments with a tracker such as Comet ML, W&B, MLflow or Neptune to compare and pick a model (3. Experiment tracking).
Test data, model and code with pytest; run six test types: unit, integration, system, acceptance, regression, stress; regression applies at all levels (4. Testing).

Model tests: check tensor shapes, loss falls after a batch, overfit a small batch toward 0 loss, run on CPU and GPU, test early stopping and checkpoints; run costly ones only when model code changes (4. Testing).
Behavioural tests per CheckList: invariance, directional, minimum functionality (4. Testing).
Log everything with origin tags; track system metrics (latency, throughput, error rates, CPU/GPU, memory) and model metrics over sliding windows, not cumulatively (5. Monitoring).

Without labels, use drift tests as proxy metrics: reference window (training data) vs test window (production); KS for continuous, chi-squared for categorical, dimensionality reduction plus MMD for embeddings (5. Monitoring).
Tune thresholds and p-values to avoid false-positive alarm floods; before retraining check data validity, schema change and isolated outliers (5. Monitoring, Alerts).
Track dataset version and config per trained model and seed every random process (6. Reproducibility).
